 How eCommerce platforms are fighting for Malaysia's 11.11 shoppers
 published
 11 November 2026
 author
 Claudia Khaw

 Is 11.11 still relevant in Malaysia when double-day and payday sales happen every month? The numbers from last year say yes. 
 According to Criteo's 2026 Year-End Shopping Decoded report , Malaysia recorded a 155% increase in sales during Singles' Day 2025, the strongest uplift across Southeast Asia. The shopping event also drove a 130% increase in first-time buyers across the region, making it the strongest customer acquisition opportunity of the year-end sale season. 
 Even though there are sale events happening every month, 11.11 for many Malaysians still means a chance to finally check out the items that have been sitting in their carts. And for others, it’s an annual ritual of stacking vouchers, hunting for flash deals and trying to make every ringgit go a little further.
 But as 11.11 becomes a fixture in Malaysia's eCommerce calendar, the competition among platforms is no longer just about who can offer the steepest discount. Shopping platforms are increasingly using entertainment, celebrity partnerships, livestreams and technology to give consumers more reasons to engage with their campaigns.
 Here’s how Malaysia's major eCommerce players are capturing consumers' attention and spending power in 2026. 
 Don't miss: Beyond discounts, what's driving Southeast Asia's Singles' Day surge? 
 Lazada: RM11 deals and surprise boxes 
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lazada Malaysia (Ecart Services Malaysia Sdn Bhd) (@lazada_my) 
 This year, Lazada Malaysia has gone for a tried and true format with its “Biggest sale of the year” campaign along with live commerce. 
 "The idea is to make 'Biggest sale of the year' feel unmistakably big," a representative from Lazada Malaysia told A+M. "11.11 is already one of the most familiar dates in retail, so the challenge is not simply awareness. It is making the occasion feel exciting, distinctive and worth participating in again."
 To establish that, Lazada Malaysia is focuing on three things: timing, deals and trust. . 
 From 7 to 13 November, the platform's 11.11 sale features surprise boxes from RM11, campaign vouchers of up to RM1,000 and flash sales offering discounts of up to 90%. 
 The RM11 deals are scheduled to drop at selected times, with the first taking place the day before on 10 November at 8pm. Shoppers can also access timed seller vouchers, alongside other promotions throughout the campaign.
 The reason for starting the sale earlier is to give shoppers more time to browse, compare, collect vouchers and prepare their carts. The idea is to shift 11.11 away from rushed, last-minute buying towards more confident deal planning.
 Lazada Malaysia also wants shoppers to be more savvy, as its 2026 eCommerce Savvy ShopperReport showed that only one in five Malaysian onlin eshoppers surveyed qualified as such.
 "The goal is to make checking a purchase as natural as searching for a deal. A low price may attract attention, but genuine value also comes from knowing what you are buying, who you are buying from and what protection you have after checkout," the representative said. 
 This year, brands played a bigger role in the campaign story. Lazada Malaysia said that trusted local and global names helped shape what shoppers discovered throughout 11.11. The platform had its first collaboration with HABIB to produce a limited-edition one-gram Lazzie gold bar, with only 500 pieces available. 
 Other participating brands include Dyson, Fan Beauty and Jean Perry, spanning categories such as home and living, beauty, fashion and electronics.
 For its live commerce efforts, Lazada is doing an “All star live stream” featuring live sellers with notable followings. 
 Shopee: RM11 million and same-day delivery 
 Shopee Malaysia is tapping into the star power of two Malaysian entertainment icons, Aina Abdul and Dato' Sri Aliff Syukri. The two came together in a duet promoting Shopee’s “11.11 big sale”. 
 This year, the platform is offering shoppers a RM11 million voucher giveaway alongside its "Buy today, get today" proposition.
 The campaign is stretched out beyond just the single day. It began on 26 October and will be happening until 12 November. The campaign also features daily Shopee VIP vouchers offering up to 30% off and Shopee Live sessions where shoppers can watch and win vouchers. 
 Other highlights include its "Lagi murah" deals and RM1,111 “Knockout vouchers”. Livestreams and interactive promotions are also a part of the sales strategy. 
 TikTok Shop: Livestreams and concerts 
 TikTok Shop is putting livestream commerce in focus this 11.11, as the platform continues to build on the role of creators and real-time shopping experiences in Malaysia's eCommerce landscape.
 Its “11.11 Mega syok sale” began on 1 November with various deals, free shipping and special brand promotions. 
 On the night of November 10, the campaign culminated in its “11.11 Mega syok concert” which saw the attendance of singers and entertainers. Dato' Fazley Yaakob and Dato’ Seri Vida were present and got engaged at the very event with a drone show proposal. 
 The approach builds on TikTok Shop's broader push into discovery-led commerce, where shoppers can encounter products through videos, creator recommendations and livestreams before making a purchase.
 The platform has also committed RM250 million in cumulative support for local sellers and creators in 2026, including through its JomLokal Booster 2.0 initiative.
 Taobao: AI-powered shopping and cross-border returns 
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by 淘宝大马站 | Taobao Malaysia (@taobao.my) 
 Taobao Malaysia is using this year's 11.11 campaign to spotlight both celebrity-led engagement and improvements to the cross-border shopping experience.
 The platform's campaign features Chinese actor Zhang Linghe, with a themed app interface, daily treasure hunts and opportunities to redeem vouchers and exclusive merchandise. Taobao has also brought the campaign offline through activations at LaLaport Kuala Lumpur and Xiamen University Malaysia in October.
 Beyond the celebrity partnership, Taobao is introducing AI-powered features intended to help shoppers navigate its extensive product catalogue. These include AI try-on, an AI shopping assistant, AI product insights and voice-assisted product search.
 The platform is also expanding its local return network through a collaboration with J&T Express, with plans to introduce more than 1,400 return drop-off points nationwide from November. This is intended to make returning eligible cross-border purchases easier without requiring consumers to ship items internationally.
 On the promotional front, Taobao is offering free shipping on eligible products across more than 400 million listings, including all fashion items, alongside sitewide discounts of up to 15% and other campaign incentives.
 The campaign runs from 20 October to 13 November.
 The various platforms’ approach to 11.11 show that price remains a major draw. However, the campaigns also highlights how 11.11 is used as a brand building event that keeps shoppers coming back even beyond the sales season.
